concerns.text: Task T026 validates SC-003 by measuring the CI width of the 'water mixing ratio distribution' using Kaplan-Meier. However, SC-003 explicitly defines the robustness metric as the '95% CI width for the correlation' (i.e., the Kendall's tau coefficient). The task measures the wrong statistical object, failing to verify the success criterion defined in the spec.

Task T031 implements a 'post-hoc power analysis' based on 'actual achieved sample size' without anchoring the test to the specific effect size required by SC-004. SC-004 mandates power ≥ 0.8 for detecting a 'moderate correlation (|tau| ≥ 0.3)'. A generic post-hoc analysis without this fixed effect size threshold does not satisfy the pre-study power requirement, constituting a semantic weakening of the success criterion.

Task T027 implements a fallback to 'Survival Regression (Cox PH or AFT)' if VIF > 5. The plan.md 'Complexity Tracking' table explicitly rejects this path, stating 'Standard Tobit yields unstable coefficients if VIF > 5' and authorizing a 'Ridge Regression Fallback' instead. Switching to Cox PH (a hazard model) for a continuous censored outcome (mixing ratio) without spec authorization violates the planned methodology and introduces unverified statistical assumptions.

Task T035 introduces a 'Methane Interference Check' and a 'contamination score' threshold (>0.5) to flag/exclude spectra. Neither the spec nor the plan authorizes a methane exclusion criterion or a contamination score threshold. This introduces a silent selection bias (scope creep) that alters the sample composition without a requirement to justify the exclusion, violating the 'ALL available spectra' mandate of FR-001 and the uniformity principle.

Task T011c defines classification logic using radius cutoffs (Radius > 0.8 R_Jup, etc.) for 'stratification'. While the task notes this is for metadata, the logic is embedded in the download/parsing step. FR-001 requires downloading 'ALL available spectra' matching planet type criteria. There is a semantic risk that the implementation of these cutoffs in the parsing logic could inadvertently filter the dataset or bias the 'ALL available' retrieval, weakening the FR-001 constraint.
